::: {#rem-contradiction-template}
#### The shape of a proof by contradiction

A proof by contradiction (@def-proof-by-contradiction) of a proposition $P$ has this shape:

> | Suppose $\neg P$.
> | $\vdots$
> | Therefore $C$ and $\neg C$.

Two things differ from a proof by contrapositive (@rem-contrapositive-template).
$P$ need not be a conditional.
And the proof does not know $C$ in advance:
any proposition $C$ for which the argument derives both $C$ and $\neg C$ will do.

:::
